_comment: Copy this file to <your-submission-folder>/submission.json and fill it in. Every field below except _comment and notes is required -- cbench community-validate refuses a submission missing any of them.
_model_comment: The exact tag your endpoint calls this model, verbatim -- the same string every CSV filename in this submission must contain (cbench community-validate checks this).
_date_comment: The date you ran these trials, not the date you opened the PR.
hardware_summary: e.g. RTX 4080 16GB VRAM, 64GB system RAM, Windows 11
_endpoint_comment: Runtime and version -- sampling defaults and quant handling differ between runtimes and versions, and this is exactly the kind of thing ARCHITECTURE.md's own "how not to fool yourself" section warns can confound a comparison.
cbench_version: output of `pip show openllm-cbench`, or the git commit hash you ran from
notes: Optional free text -- anything unusual about the run: a config_overrides you had to set, a caveat this model needed, trials you excluded and why, etc.
_checksums_comment: Optional -- {relative CSV path: sha256}, one entry per CSV in this submission. `cbench community-package` fills this in automatically; leave it out entirely for a hand-assembled submission (that's not an error, just unverifiable). Don't add a partial one by hand -- cbench community-validate treats a listed-but-missing file, or a checksum that doesn't match the file on disk, as a real problem.
